reviews.author: Christy S.
reviews.text:
Great staff! We reserved 2 tent sites, unseen in person,(online photos), with power/ water. We arrived on a Monday, with the following Thursday as our departure day.
Unfortunately the weather decided to give us a challenge as it rained hard on Monday, we checked in and got directions to our sites. We pull up and discover that it had(&would continue for another 18 hours) to pour down rain.. like big heavy rain drops!
Both our sites were flooded.. like ankle deep water, small lakes exactly where our tents were supposed to go.. the only place they could be set up actually. I found all the tent sights to be on the small size. A larger tent(like anything that sleeps more than 4 would not fit any sites here.. unless set up on the pavement.  Then you can't anchor it down.)
Anyway, so back to the office and advised of the flooded sites. The ranger took a map and searched thru his computer until he found a selection of available sites next to each other for our reservation requirements to choose from. He said go drive the loops and look at the sites once we found the two that would work for us to come back and he got them switched for us.
The next day the rain wasn't as bad and the mosquitoes started looking for their food..aka us!
Make sure to bring bug spray or better still.. use the premithin spray that  lasts 6 weeks or 6 laundry washing on your tents, clothing, shoes, ect. Do not spray it on ur clothes while wearing ur clothes.. follow directions! We had 40% deer and it slowed them down a little.. not much. We also had the thermocell misting machine mosquitoe repellent  and 2 large costco brand citronella candles and finally the bug repellent sticks that you light, stick in the ground around ur site and it slowly burns.. we still got attacked by the mosquitoes  so be aware that there is an issue with the mosquitoes here!
Everywhere but the actual beach where the wind seems to keep them away.
Otherwise, all the attractions at the park are great. The rv sites Great, staff, awesome, plenty of hot water for showers.
Have fun in town lots of shops, attractions to do locally.

reviews.author: Carl O.
reviews.text: Fun riding the trails. Bathrooms/showers were a little rough but lots of hot water. Came during fishing season, wouldn't suggest it unless you are fishing too. Loop E has showers.

reviews.author: JoAnn D.
reviews.text:
Beautiful escape from city-life, just a few miles out. Quiet, peaceful, and easy to navigate.

Nice pull through available for bigger rigs.

$10 to dump, electric and water at the sites.

Elk roaming freely throughout the park, drive slowly and cautiously.

Restrooms close by, firepits and picnic tables all around.

This site shown is Loop F, #235.

reviews.author: Cathy O.
reviews.text: Wonderful campground! Basic/clean/free hot showers. Paved bike paths, playgrounds, hiking trails. We had a nice, relatively private site : 236 F. Not perfectly level but worked fine. Laundromat just outside the park.

reviews.author: Hal K.
reviews.text:
Very nice campground that is well laid out. Close to a lot of different things to do. We used it as a base to explore the area South to Tillamook and over to Astoria, and also to the Washington side of Fort Canby. We especially liked Astoria with the Sunday market and the Astoria column at sunset.
One of the few negatives is the presence of mosquitoes near our campsite on h loop must be pretty boggy in the middle and nearby
The other negative is the cost of the sites with the addition of of fees I.e daily fees and markup for non-residents. This is not a cheap campground to stay at. But relative to the KOA across the street, it's still cheaper.

reviews.author: Ant
reviews.text: Level site. Paved. We had water and electricity. There is dump on site. You could buy fire wood and ice. Bicycle rentals on site. Lots of paved cycle paths. You can cycle to beach as well as 4x4 vehicle beach access. Washrooms clean. Lots of hot water. No pay at showers. Garbage disposal and recycling on site.
reviews.title: Beautiful State Park

reviews.author: Nathan Helder
reviews.text: We only stayed 1 night and wished we could have stayed longer. The campsite was clean and level. We enjoyed driving onto the beach with our truck. We didn't get a chance to bicycle around, but the paved trails were fantastic. We would come back!
reviews.title: Great place - lots to do

reviews.author: Richard n Mary
reviews.text: Convenient location for many local attractions such as Fort Stevens, Fort Clatsop, Columbia River Museum, City of Astoria, great beaches, and much more. Our site was spacious, level, and included 30 amp electric hookup, as well as table and fire ring. The restrooms were very clean, as were the free showers with hot water.
reviews.title: Convenient Campground to visit local attractions

reviews.author: rls1936
reviews.text: Easy check-in, just stop by the ranger station. Contrary to other reviews, mosquitoes were not bad, I think they sprayed recently. No noise, except lots of kids playing and bike riding in the loop, but that's expected until school starts. Had deer walking through our camp site, and saw a bull elk on the way in.
reviews.title: Beautiful Park, Close to the beach

reviews.author: Paul
reviews.text: Great location and beautiful park. Sites were large and separated and easy enough for back-in and pull throughs. We stayed for 2 nights. Only drawback was we had zero bars for AT&T and Verizon (others say they have coverage, but we were not able to find any). We were working remotely and had to head to Winchester by 5am for some ET video meetings. The benefit was that we saw several elk early in the morning just hanging out by the roads. Overall a great park and I wish we had more (non-working) time to visit.
reviews.title: Very nice State Park

reviews.author: Murphysmom11
reviews.text: We stayed here for 2 nights in April. We originally had 5 nights reserved, but found an opening at Cannon Beach RV Resort and moved there after 2 nights. The good - Beautiful park with nice large sites. So much to do, trails and beach access. Loved seeing the Elk hanging out by the front park ranger station.
reviews.title: Beautiful Park but some negatives

reviews.author: The_Travel_Family123
reviews.text: This is a great well maintained campground and I am glad we visited. The historic fort was cool to see. Sites were level and spacious with water and electrical hookups. Be warned, the mosquitoes that thrive in the streams along the paths are from hell itself! No repellent will work against them.
reviews.title: My favorite camping park! So much to do!

reviews.author: Renée H
reviews.text: The paths around the fort were good, and markers gave a brief description. The campground sites were ok, and the bathrooms and showers were clean and very nice. There were a lot of mosquitoes in June.

reviews.author: Barbara S
reviews.text: My husband and I have camped at Fort Stevens several times in the past two years and it has become one of our favorite "go to" places on the beach. The park has a little bit of everything--hiking trails, biking trails, beach, historic monuments, the jetty, and one of the largest campgrounds in any Oregon state park including yurts and cabins. In the off season, it is easy to get a site on short notice, but for the summer season, it is best to plan far ahead to get a camping site. Some of the sites are very private and some are not. We love this park where we can plan a "stay-cation" weekend. However, nearby Astoria has plenty to offer with restaurants, museums, and shopping. The Peter Iredale shipwreck is still listed as one of the top sights at Fort Stevens, but not much remains now. However, the beach will always be there. Life is good on the beach!

reviews.author: NNKELLEY
reviews.text: There is SO MUCH to do at Ft. Stevens. There are excellent biking paths, so nearly everyone brings a bike so they can get to all of the fun things there are to do at Ft. Stevens. From the campground you can bike to the beach where you can do all of the normal beachy things in addition to checking out the remains of the Peter Iredale shipwreck. You can also ride your bike to a nearby lake where there is a designated beach for the kids to splash around in or, if you brought your own kayaks/canoes and/or fishing poles, you could do that, too. Let's not forget the actual fort. Yes, there is an old fort that has a small museum as well as the remains from what is left over from the fort that was decommissioned after World War II...lots of history there. If you want to stay at Ft. Stevens you can stay in a cabin, a yurt, you can tent camp, and they also a have LOT of spots for RVs. We have been there twice and have stayed in a cabin both times. The cabins have bathrooms with a shower and toilet. There is also a kitchen with a sink, a refrigerator and a microwave. Outside each cabin there is a fire pit and an electric drill.

reviews.author: Jarod C.
reviews.text: If you have kids, and/or just like to immerse yourself in the history of the area you're camping in, Fort Stevens State Park is the right place. For the casual state park camper: Tons of campsites with a variety of size and accommodation options, rentable cabins and yurts, excellent bathroom and shower facilities, close to the ocean, and bike paths galore. For the history buff: The wreckage of the Peter Iredale; year-round military displays at the military museum and information center; the only Civil War-era earthen fort on the west coast; multiple turn-of-the-century, concrete artillery gun batteries; underground tours of a gun battery that served as a World War II command center. Fort Clatsop, the last encampment of Lewis and Clark's Corps of Discovery before embarking on their return trip east to St. Louis.
reviews.title: Campground Camping with Kids? Look No Further!
